visual.general_description: Twelve-lead color electrocardiogram tracing on pink grid paper with lead names printed beside each row.
visual.detailed_description: Twelve-lead color electrocardiogram on pink millimeter-style grid paper, arranged in two columns of six rows. The left column carries the limb leads I, II, III, aVR, aVL and aVF and the right column the precordial leads V1 through V6, each lead name printed beside its row. A small rectangular calibration-style mark sits at the left edge of each left-column row. Every row shows a repeating narrow spike followed by a smaller rounded wave; the spikes are tall and upright in V2 through V4 with rounded waves after them, and small or downward in V1, aVR and parts of the limb leads. The spacing of the repeated complexes looks even across the rows. No printed heart rate, paper speed, gain, name, date or other text is visible beyond the lead names.

visual.general_description: Three stacked grayscale ECG strips labelled a, b and c on a dotted grid.
visual.detailed_description: Three horizontally oriented grayscale ECG strips stacked vertically, labelled with lowercase letters a, b and c at the upper left of each strip, on a dotted grid. Strip a shows an irregular run of wide large deflections after the first beats; strip b shows regular narrow spikes each followed by a tall rounded, somewhat pointed wave; strip c shows regular narrow spikes each followed by a lower rounded wave. No lead names, rate, paper speed, gain or time scale are printed.

panels.general_description: Top strip of a stacked three-strip ECG figure: wide irregular large deflections after the first beats.
panels.detailed_description: Strip a: a single dark trace on a dotted grid. It begins with a flat stretch and a narrow spike with a small rounded wave, then a second tall narrow spike followed by a broad dome, then a run of repeated large broad deflections that go both up and down and look wide and closely spaced, with amplitude growing toward the right end. The regular narrow-spike-plus-small-wave pattern of the first beats is no longer visible in the later part of the strip. No lead name, rate, scale or other text is printed besides the panel letter.

evidence.quote: a VT developed approximately 20 min after the end of mannitol administration.
